title: When Does Sycophancy Degrade into Misinformation? A Severity Ladder Study
original_idea: Design a severity ladder of user pressure from mild agreement to harmful advice confirmation. Measure where models are on the ladder and what pushes them further.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Moderate theory of impact: identifying severity thresholds helps regulators set safety thresholds. However, the connection to actionable interventions is less direct than mechanism-focused work.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Well-suited for beginners: designing prompts with varying pressure levels and measuring model responses is straightforward. Can be done via API with medium compute. The severity ladder is an intuitive framework.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The severity ladder is a well-defined experimental structure. Testing a fixed set of pressure levels on a few models is very doable in 30 hours. Clear deliverable: a per-model severity profile.

novelty.reasoning: Sycophancy research has substantially advanced in 2024-2025. The SYCON benchmark measures multi-turn conversational sycophancy with 'Turn of Flip' metrics. SycEval (arxiv 2502.08177) provides comprehensive sycophancy evaluation. Research on medical sycophancy (Nature Digital Medicine, 2025) measures compliance rates up to 100% under illogical pressure. The 'severity ladder' framing is novel as a specific experimental construct, but the underlying phenomenon of escalating pressure leading to capitulation is well-documented. The idea's main contribution would be systematizing existing findings into a graded framework.
